blocks.text: A raw in-place sort would change the caller's array and detach values from their original positions. A legal adaptation pairs each value with its index or sorts an equivalent copy, adding O(n) construction time and O(n) extra state before O(n log n) sorting. Original indices generally cannot be reconstructed from values alone when duplicates exist. The transfer rule is to account for every wrapper, copy, index map, or normalization required to make a mechanism legal; adaptations are part of the strategy, not free implementation details.

messages.text: This model describes a different mutability contract and hides the copied representation. It becomes accurate only when the input is privately mutable and original positions are irrelevant.

feedback.reason: Preserving mutation and identity contracts requires an explicit copied/indexed representation. Its construction and storage belong in the candidate's cost.

blocks.text: Cost models must state their assumptions and guarantee semantics. A conventional hash table often performs expected constant-time operations under suitable hashing and input assumptions, but pathological collisions can degrade a sequence of operations. Sorting offers a deterministic comparison bound in the stated model. If the product contract accepts expected latency, hashing may still win; under an explicit worst-case requirement, it fails that boundary. The transfer rule is to compare amortized, expected, average, and worst-case claims only after matching them to the required guarantee.

blocks.text: Time and space are separate constraints. The input already exists, but the hash table adds millions of entries with allocation and load-factor overhead; that extra state can exceed a hard memory cap. In-place sorting reuses the input representation and may need only recursion or library workspace, at the cost of O(n log n) comparisons. Once the hash candidate is infeasible, it leaves the comparison set regardless of its expected time. The transfer rule is to apply hard resource bounds as gates, then rank the remaining legal and feasible candidates.

blocks.text: Complexity must reflect the full output contract. When k can be Θ(n²), the natural model is O(preprocessing + search overhead + k), and the worst case inherits the quadratic output term. Ignoring emission would compare candidates against a different problem that returns only existence or count. The transfer rule is to use output-sensitive notation whenever the answer may contain a variable number of records, paths, intervals, matches, or witnesses.

blocks.text: Static preprocessing costs can become repeated maintenance costs when data changes. The prefix array itself remains O(n) state, but each point update invalidates all later prefix entries under this naive maintenance policy, so rebuilding costs O(n) per update. The total lifecycle is O(n) + u·O(n) + q·O(1). Quoting O(1) queries alone can make the strategy look attractive even when updates dominate. The transfer rule is to model build, query, update, and rebuild frequencies separately for every preprocessed representation.

blocks.text: Strategies are compared as complete lifecycles. The sorted-copy candidate performs O(n) copying, O(n log n) sorting, and O(n) pointer movement, dominated by O(n log n), while retaining O(n) auxiliary records. The direct pair scan uses little extra memory but O(n²) time. Neither time nor space alone determines the result; resource constraints decide whether the trade-off is acceptable. The transfer rule is to include setup and preservation adaptations whenever an appealing inner loop is preceded by sorting, indexing, copying, or transformation.

constraints: The array is static.

blocks.text: A cost model must include every lifecycle phase. Define P[0] = 0 and build P[i + 1] = P[i] + a[i] for all n values, which costs O(n) time. Each inclusive query [l, r] returns P[r + 1] − P[l] with a constant number of accesses and arithmetic operations, so q queries add O(q). The n + 1 stored prefix values require O(n) extra space. Therefore total time is O(n) + q·O(1) = O(n + q), not O(1) with hidden setup and not O(nq) with an invented rescan. The transfer rule is to express total cost as setup + operations × per-operation cost and keep persistent index space separate from input storage.

feedback.reason: The one-time prefix construction visits n values and each of q queries uses constant work, for O(n + q) total time and O(n) extra state.
